tasks.short: Study and interpret religious doctrine and tradition

steps.what: Study and interpret religious laws, doctrines and traditions in their community context

tasks.design: Retain study and interpretation with clergy using source texts in {DOCS}. A generated explanation can be fluent while missing denominational meaning; this task supplies no separate repetitive clerical operation to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interpretation depends on tradition, context and reflective understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Text access helps study without establishing a substitute for it.
tasks.still_hard: Different authorities may understand a passage or practice differently.
tasks.human_edge: Clergy take responsibility for interpretation within the community's tradition.
tasks.altitude: Study responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify an interpretation for teaching preparation

evidence.claim: Retaining doctrinal study and interpretation is an E1 assessment from model knowledge, consistent with the digest's human-work boundary.

assumptions: Boundary is study and interpretation, excluding producing lessons, sermons or administrative records.
No structured doctrinally-correct flag is assumed; clergy interpret existing source texts directly.
Retain native source access; no custom interpretation tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. Disagree with the amplification prior where it removes reflection itself.
unknowns: Tradition, recognised authorities and source access
research_questions: Which interpretations require consultation with an authorised religious scholar?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; reading and interpretation retain full time without a guessed summary-production baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Respond to emergency or crisis assistance requests

steps.what: Respond to assistance requests during emergencies or crises and arrange appropriate support
outputs: appropriate specialist referral or emergency contact

tasks.design: Retain immediate pastoral response and recognition of needs beyond clergy competence. Existing support contacts in {DOCS} can aid referral; no automated crisis judgement is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Urgent needs require presence, listening and contextual escalation.
tasks.enabler_now: Administrative software does not replace the pastoral encounter.
tasks.still_hard: A request may conceal immediate danger or a need for qualified care.
tasks.human_edge: Clergy build trust while recognising when specialist or emergency help is needed.
tasks.altitude: Crisis-response responsibility and time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Make an appropriate support referral with necessary consent or authority

evidence.claim: Retaining personal pastoral crisis response is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is clergy response and referral coordination, excluding specialist treatment and emergency-service labour.
No free structured crisis severity or referral eligibility flag is assumed.
Existing support procedures remain; no custom triage tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; local safeguarding duties require confirmation.
unknowns: Safeguarding arrangements and available specialist services
research_questions: Which situations require immediate emergency or safeguarding escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; personal response and referral coordination keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct special ceremonies including weddings, funerals or confirmations according to the religious tradition

tasks.design: Retain personal conduct of ceremonies. Prepared materials in {DOCS} support the occasion; generating those materials or booking the venue belongs to separate preparation work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The ceremony's meaning depends on authorised presence and personal participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Administrative tools do not conduct the pastoral ceremony.
tasks.still_hard: Grief, family circumstances or participant needs can require sensitive adaptation.
tasks.human_edge: Clergy provide presence and guide participants through a significant occasion.
tasks.altitude: Ceremonial authority and attendance time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify participant support needs for a ceremony

evidence.claim: Retaining personal ceremony conduct is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is conducting the ceremony, excluding planning, legal registration and printed material preparation.
The existing preparation process supplies the ceremony order; no structured eligible-participant flag or automatic religious authorisation is assumed.
Retain existing ceremony materials; no custom tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; religious and national civil requirements need local confirmation.
research_questions: Which participant circumstances require personal pastoral preparation before the ceremony?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; ceremony delivery retains all time without importing booking or writing work.

tasks.short: Devise ways to expand congregational membership

steps.what: Listen to community needs and frame objectives for expanding congregational membership
Develop alternative outreach ideas addressing the membership objectives

loop.purpose: Suggest varied outreach approaches for clergy consideration
loop.input: Clergy-written non-identifying brief with mission, audience needs and resource limits
loop.output: Three candidate approaches labelled as proposals
loop.check: Clergy checks each idea against the brief, tradition, actual resources and community dignity; rejects invented local facts
loop.stop: One draft; unsuitable or unsupported ideas return to manual development
loop.why_not_simpler: Open-ended alternatives require language synthesis; fixed templates cannot generate useful variations for different community needs

steps.what: Assess outreach ideas with community context and choose recommendations for membership growth

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting aid in {DOCS} to suggest three outreach options from a clergy-written, non-identifying brief. Clergy retain listening and contextual selection; council authorisation and delivery remain outside this proposal-generation task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing varied initial options can repeat familiar approaches.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded language draft can provide alternatives for critical review.
tasks.still_hard: An appealing idea may not suit the local community or religious mission.
tasks.human_edge: Clergy know the relationships and judge whether an approach is respectful and feasible.
tasks.altitude: Compare more varied initial ideas with unchanged outreach decision authority.

reach.task: Compare outreach options against practical programme constraints

evidence.claim: A bounded aid for initial outreach ideas is an E1 design from model knowledge; the digest supplies no measured membership-growth or labour-saving case.

assumptions: Boundary is developing recommendations, excluding member profiling, council approval, publicity and programme delivery.
Clergy s1 produces the brief covering non-identifying audience needs, mission, resources and constraints with capture included in35 hours; absent or sensitive inputs return to manual ideation.
Try existing document drafting support before custom code; do not submit pastoral accounts or member records.
No growth outcome is assumed; extra activities need separate capacity and consent assessment.
unknowns: Approved drafting environment and actual initial-ideation effort
research_questions: Do reviewed drafts save initial development time without reducing community listening or feasibility scrutiny?

incremental.description: Review prompt behaviour and unsuitable suggestions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90 gross10 minus4 upkeep gives net6. E1 scenario: additional rejection or redrafting lowers net to0-4; community listening and final judgement retain full time.

reach: Compare outreach feasibility with religious activities directors
